attributes.body_ja:
助詞（じょし）「こそ」には、特定（とくてい）の語（ご）を強調（きょうちょう）し「まさにそれが理由（りゆう）だ」と示（しめ）す働（はたら）きがありますが、動詞（どうし）のテ形（けい）と組（く）み合（あ）わせた「〜てこそ」は (A) を強調（きょうちょう）し「(B) は (A) によって初（はじ）めて成（な）り立（た）つ」ことを表（あらわ）します。この表現（ひょうげん）は「(A) してはじめて (B)」「(A) しなければ (B) しない」「(A) するまで (B) しない」のような意味（いみ）合（あ）いで使（つか）われます。

この表現（ひょうげん）は、話（はな）し手（て）の意見（いけん）や価値観（かちかん）、または状況（じょうきょう）の理解（りかい）に基（もと）づいて「(A) が (B) の結果（けっか）や評価（ひょうか）を決（き）める」というニュアンスで使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。
attributes.body:
In a similar way to how the particle こそ highlights a particular word as being the 'precise' or 'exact' reason for something, its combination with the て-form of a verb will indicate that (B) is absolutely reliant on (A). This reliance can be translated in several different ways, and will usually become clear in the (B) part of sentences. Standard interpretations include 'only if (A), (B)', 'unless (A), (B)', or 'until (A), (B)'.

The reliance that (B) has on (A) can be translated in several different ways, but the most common interpretations are that (A) will determine either the outcome, assessment, or evaluation of (B), based on the speaker's opinion, values, or understanding of the situation.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Difference between てこそ and からこそ
接続・意味・使い方・例文
verb +て + こそ:  emphasizing certain condition/reason

attributes.body: Both use the emphatic こそ but differ by verb form. ～ばこそ is conditional, meaning only if (A), then (B), as in 忙しければこそ 'precisely because you're busy'. ～てこそ focuses on completion, meaning only after (A) happens, then (B), as in 苦労してこそ成功がある ('Only after hardship comes success'). ～ばこそ can introduce a hypothetical condition, while ～てこそ emphasizes the actual realization of (A).

second_relatable.title: ～てこそ
second_relatable.meaning: Only if, Because, By, Unless, Until

attributes.body: These are both emphatic expressions that can be used in similar contexts to express 'it's entirely because of (A) that (B)'. あっての is narrower in use, saying that something was possible only because something else 'exists', e.g. 皆さんの努力あっての成功だ ('This success is entirely because of everyone's effort.'). てこそ can be used with a wider variety of verbs, such as 留学してこそ学べること ('things you can only learn by studying abroad'.).

first_relatable.title: あっての
first_relatable.meaning: Exist only because of or due to, Owe everything to

second_relatable.title: ～てこそ
second_relatable.meaning: Only if, Because, By, Unless, Until

attributes.body: Both からこそ and ～てこそ emphasize cause and effect, but they differ in nuance. からこそ highlights a specific reason with a strong emphasis, e.g. 努力したからこそ合格できた ('I was able to pass precisely because I worked hard'). In contrast, ～てこそ indicates that only after a certain condition is fulfilled can something else happen, e.g. 努力してこそ意味がある ('It only has meaning after putting in effort').

second_relatable.title: ～てこそ
second_relatable.meaning: Only if, Because, By, Unless, Until

attributes.body: Both involve the same こそ, but one attaches to nouns and the other to verb + て form. こそ emphasizes a specific word or element, often to contrast or highlight, e.g. 彼こそできる ('He, if nobody else, can do it.'). In contrast, ～てこそ focuses a condition that must be met for something to be true, e.g. 大人になってこそ分かる 'understand only after becoming an adult'.
